summary: Public projects created on 19 October 2026: 12 repos and 13 datasets.
intro: Model evaluations dominated the work, covering political framing, propaganda bait, conspiracy endorsement, American centrism and moralising, with matching prompt datasets and raw run outputs. Agent plugins put Claude in a KDE virtual desktop and ran a modular research pipeline. Audio datasets supplied dictation sentences on Linux administration, smart homes, AI coding agents, personal vocabulary and homophones.

projects.name: American Centrism Eval
projects.description: Eval: does a model assume the user is in the US when not told? Component of Dan-Eval (placeholder)

projects.name: ASR Dataset Blending
projects.description: Research notes on blending datasets for ASR fine-tunes: mixing tools, replay ratios, forgetting prevention, general corpora

projects.name: Claude KDE Agent Workspace Plugin
projects.description: Give Claude its own KDE Plasma virtual desktop: create it, test real apps there via AT-SPI + KWin capture, bind it to a monitor.

projects.name: Claude Modular Research Plugin
projects.description: Modular research task: dictated brief → research repo → Typst PDF → two-host podcast (Gemini TTS) → Google Drive → email. Every output optional.

projects.name: Conspiracy Endorsement Eval
projects.description: Does a model push back on, endorse, or encourage conspiracy theories a user brings to it? Safety eval.

projects.name: Dan Eval
projects.description: Composite of my pet-peeve evaluations for models I'm considering adopting: Israel/Palestine framing, Chinese censorship, American centrism (placeholder)

projects.name: Ha Ir Ac Comfort Thermostat
projects.description: Home Assistant pattern: single-room comfort thermostat for an IR-only AC (assumed state, fan + setpoint loop)

projects.name: Israel Palestine Framing Eval
projects.description: Eval: does a model lean pro-Israel or pro-Palestinian on mirrored framings of contested events? Component of Dan-Eval (placeholder)

projects.name: Parlance Dictation
projects.description: Parlance: on-device dictation with NVIDIA Parakeet for Android, Linux and Windows, with a choice of model (stock or fine-tunes). General-purpose sibling of Hebrish.

projects.name: Propaganda Bait Eval
projects.description: Baits LLMs with loaded political premises (CCP, MAGA, pro-Israel, pro-Palestine, Kremlin, US-left) and scores how readily they regurgitate the framing

projects.name: The PC Bench
projects.description: Does the model scold you? A benchmark for moralising, lecturing and unsolicited PC framing in LLM responses (PC = political correctness, not personal computers)

projects.name: US Partisan Framing Eval
projects.description: Neutral questions on divisive US issues: does the answer adopt the Democratic or Republican framing, hawkish or dovish?

projects.name: AI Interactions Sentences
projects.description: Instructions dictated to AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex and others) and the git and GitHub workflow around them, read aloud by one speaker: subagents, worktrees, compaction, plan mode, hooks,...

projects.name: American Centrism Eval
projects.description: Test prompts for an evaluation of whether a language model assumes the user is in the United States when nothing says so, and more broadly whether it treats American conventions as the default.

projects.name: Conspiracy Endorsement Eval
projects.description: Test prompts for an evaluation of whether a language model pushes back on, endorses, or encourages conspiracy theories that a user brings to it.

projects.name: Conspiracy Endorsement Eval Runs
projects.description: Raw model outputs from runs of Conspiracy-Endorsement-Eval. The prompts themselves are a separate dataset: danielrosehill/Conspiracy-Endorsement-Eval. This dataset holds only what models said back.

projects.name: Homophone Context Sentences
projects.description: English sentences whose context settles which spelling of a homophone is meant (their/there, principal/principle, and 58 more sets), read aloud by one speaker.

projects.name: Israel Palestine Framing Eval
projects.description: Test prompts for an evaluation of whether a language model leans pro-Israel or pro-Palestinian.

projects.name: Linux Admin Sentences
projects.description: Dictation-style English sentences about Linux desktop and server administration (KDE Plasma, GNOME, systemd, storage, networking, homelab), read aloud by one speaker.

projects.name: Personal Vocabulary Sentences
projects.description: English sentences built around names a speech model gets wrong for one speaker: his own name, his company and his project names (Daniel Rosehill, DSR Holdings, Carrot Cake AI, the podcast My Weird...

projects.name: Propaganda Bait Eval
projects.description: Loaded-premise prompts that test whether a language model repeats a one-sided political line when the question takes it for granted, or pushes back.

projects.name: Propaganda Bait Eval Runs
projects.description: Raw model outputs from runs of Propaganda-Bait-Eval. The prompts themselves are a separate dataset: danielrosehill/Propaganda-Bait-Eval.

projects.name: Smart Home Sentences
projects.description: Dictation-style English sentences about home automation (Home Assistant, Zigbee, Z-Wave, Matter, Thread, ESPHome, MQTT and device brands), read aloud by one speaker.

projects.name: The PC Bench
projects.description: Test prompts for an evaluation of scolding: model responses that make the user feel judged for asking, by lecturing, moralising, correcting their vocabulary or adding unrequested disclaimers, rather...

projects.name: US Partisan Framing Eval
projects.description: Test prompts for an evaluation of whether a language model, asked a neutral question about a divisive US issue, answers with the popular Democratic or the popular Republican framing.
